record.original_question: Can the intertwining construction for polynomials be implemented by quasiconformal surgery?

evidence.quote: Question 10. Can intertwinings be constructed with quasiconformal surgery?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f_1, f_2: \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be two monic polynomials of degrees $d_1, d_2 \geq 2$ each having a fixed point with prescribed multiplier (e.g., a common repelling or parabolic fixed point with matching combinatorial data along external rays landing there). An "intertwining" of $f_1$ and $f_2$ is a polynomial $F$ of degree $d_1 + d_2 - 1$ together with a decomposition of the filled Julia set $K(F)$ into two invariant pieces on which $F$ is conjugate to $f_1$ and $f_2$ respectively, glued along the orbit of the chosen fixed point so that the external ray combinatorics of $f_1$ and $f_2$ are matched.

Question: Can such an intertwining polynomial $F$ always be produced by quasiconformal surgery? Concretely, does there exist a construction that builds a quasiregular model map by cutting and pasting $f_1$ and $f_2$ along chosen ray pairs, equips $\mathbb{C}$ with an $F$-invariant Beltrami coefficient of norm strictly less than $1$, and then applies the measurable Riemann mapping theorem to straighten this model to a holomorphic polynomial $F$ realizing the intertwining of $f_1$ and $f_2$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of realizing the intertwining construction for polynomials via quasiconformal surgery was answered affirmatively by Epstein and Yampolsky in "Geography of the cubic connectedness locus I: Intertwining surgery" (Annales Scientifiques de l'ENS, 1999), where intertwining surgery is implemented as a quasiconformal surgery in the spirit of Branner–Douady, producing cubic (and more generally higher-degree) polynomials by intertwining two lower-degree ones.

status_evidence.title: Geography of the cubic connectedness locus: Intertwining surgery
status_evidence.snippet: Epstein and Yampolsky implement intertwining as a quasiconformal surgery to study the cubic connectedness locus.
status_evidence.claim: Intertwining of polynomials can be implemented by quasiconformal surgery, as carried out by Epstein–Yampolsky.

status_evidence.title: Quasiconformal Surgery in Holomorphic Dynamics (Branner–Fagella)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys quasiconformal surgery techniques including intertwining-type cut-and-paste constructions on polynomials.
status_evidence.claim: The intertwining construction is part of the standard quasiconformal surgery toolkit in holomorphic dynamics.
